title: multiplicative Mirror-MoE
hypothesis: A product of two low-description hidden-channel scale views can create four useful logical experts from one shared FFN, with lower payload than independent experts and better quality than hard tying.
mirror_coordinate: two binary role coordinates that multiply shared hidden scale factors channelwise
logical_multiplicity: four expert functions from s_r=(1+a_(r//2)u) elementwise-multiplied by (1+b_(r%2)v)
controls: shared FFN plus rank-2 output residual

task.routing: balanced oracle top-1 roles supplied to all methods

teacher_modes.aligned: shared FFN with hidden multiplier (1+a_i u) elementwise-multiplied by (1+b_j v), i=r//2,j=r%2

task.structure_audit: per-role MSE and hidden multiplier dispersion

development.selection_metric: mean held-out MSE across five methods and both teacher modes

fresh.access_condition: At selected learning rate, multiplicative Mirror aligned MSE <=1.25x full independent and payload <=0.80x independent; otherwise fresh remains sealed.

storage.serialization: torch.save CPU state_dict plus deterministic compact JSON config
paid_objects: multiplicative basis vectors and role scalars

success_gate: All three fresh aligned worlds: multiplicative Mirror MSE <=1.10x full independent, payload <=0.75x independent, and at least 10% lower MSE than hard tying with <=10% extra bytes. Compare explicitly to full FiLM and rank-2 residual; this is not Mirror-specific if either matches at equal/lower bytes.
failure_gate: Development access gate misses; or at least two fresh aligned worlds miss quality or bytes; or hard tie/FiLM/rank-2 matches Mirror within 10% quality at equal/lower bytes in at least two worlds.
boundaries: teacher deliberately contains factorized multiplicative scale interaction
